payload.body:
examiner (task 1): approach for the exam at fleet/tests/test_run_engine_kata_close.mjs.

One two-task sim carries legs (a) and (b): waves [[task 1, task 2]], stamp `run-12`, a fake hub of the shape test_worker_kata_env.mjs builds (getIssue/claim/patchMetadata/comment/close/addLabel over an in-memory store, every call recorded in order with the revision it answered), record naming tasks 1 and 2 at the store's revisions. Stub: impl writes its file and returns doneImpl; the reviewer PASSes task 1 and returns a blocking FIX_REQUIRED for task 2 on every round — so task 1 is the wave's one mergeable row and task 2 ends unadopted and needs-review, whether the engine's fix loop is one round or two.

(a) [M1]: among U-1's patchMetadata calls exactly one carries `work.adopted_run`, its patch deep-equals {'work.adopted_run': 12, 'work.adopted_sha': <headSha>} (integer 12, not '12'; sha from the run's `driver:wave-adopted` event in events.jsonl), its revision argument is the revision the fake last answered for U-1 before that call, and the next call for U-1 is the `close`, whose commit evidence deep-equals {type: 'commit', sha: <the same headSha>}.
(b) [M2]: the fake's store for U-2 has neither adopted key (and no patchMetadata for U-2 ever carried one) while it does carry work.attention 'needs-human'.
(c) [M3]: the same two-task run built with no kata and no kataRecord — a second fake constructed and never passed records zero calls, no `kata:` event is on the log, and the wave still adopts.
(d) [M4]: CONTRACT.md read through the Proof's own sed range (the `Kata record (engine)` line through the first `status.json:` line), asserting the Closes sentence names work.adopted_run then work.adopted_sha.

The exam calls `_engine_helpers.rig` with `kata`, which is the rig edit this task makes; at BASE the rig drops it, the engine's kataOn stays false and (a) is red on the absent patch.

examiner (task 1): exam handed in — fleet/tests/test_run_engine_kata_close.mjs, all four legs live, nothing else in the tree.

Red at BASE for one reason: the preconditions all pass (the two-task sim runs end to end, wave 1 adopts task 1, task 2 ends not-done), and the first failure is `(a) [M1] the engine patched task 1's issue with \`work.adopted_run\` exactly once … recorded for U-1 were: []` — at BASE `_engine_helpers.rig` drops the `kata` argument, so `kataOn` is false and no hub call is made at all.

Verified satisfiable: against a scratch copy of the tree carrying the minimal implementation (rig's `kata = undefined` + spread, one `kataCall('metadata', …)` before each `kataClose` in the mergeable loop, the CONTRACT Closes sentence) the exam is green, three runs in a row, and the Proof's `Run:` grep is green on that sentence. It also stays green when the patch is written WITHOUT a `drainKataPosts()` ahead of it, so leg (a)'s "immediately followed by that uid's close" and its revision reading do not pin one particular drain placement.

Two readings a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct:
- "under the revision the fake last answered for that uid" is asserted from outside as: walk the fake's call log to the stamping patch, take the revision of the last answer the fake gave for that uid before it. Reads (getIssue, the attention poll) do not bump the store, so a stray poll cannot move it.
- "immediately followed by that uid's close" is asserted on that UID's OWN call subsequence (`forUid(uid)`), not the global log: comments for the RUN issue may interleave globally, and the leg is about what the engine does to the task's issue.

Leg (b) is asserted twice over — the store for U-2 has neither key, and no patchMetadata for U-2 ever carried one — so a per-key-merge implementation that stamped the wrong issue cannot hide. Nothing is unsatisfiable.

payload.body:
Three readings the exam encodes, for whoever implements this.

1. LEG (e), "the baseline suite ... ran on a tree carrying both": read literally, this puts the reuse fold BEFORE the baseline clone is cut. The baseline clone is where the suite on the run's floor runs (run-engine.mjs ~1625-1630), and with a reuse the floor IS the reuse head — so cloneAtBase for `baseline` has to take the reuse head, not BASE. The exam snapshots each recorded `bash -lc <testCmd>` call's cwd + HEAD tree AT THE MOMENT OF THE CALL (the integration head moves later) and requires both one.txt and third.txt in the baseline clone's tree and in the integration clone's. Task Context agrees: it places the moved hub read "before the baseline suite starts".

2. "THE RUN ENDS APPROVED" is asserted as criticDecision(report).approve === true with blocking: [], completenessFindings deep-equal [], and report.tests.passed === true. Deliberately NOT coverage.complete: a reused task contributes no branch to any wave's fold (M3 excludes it), so coverage.complete is false in a reuse run by construction and would be the wrong thing to hold the implementer to.

3. LEG (f) SECOND HALF is intentionally not in the exam file. test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs enforces "no surviving sim names a sibling sim, run or merely checked for existence" — asserting the two survivor sims exist inside this file breaks that standing guard (verified: the probe went red, then green once removed). The Proof's first two `Run:` lines already RUN those two sims and grep their sentinel, which is what the leg asks for. The exam covers (f)'s contract half.

Two rig facts the exam depends on, so a later session does not re-derive them.

- The sim origin (makeParkedOrigin) advances main by a commit touching third.txt AFTER the parked base, and BASE is that tip. So `main=` in the publish-fold shape is non-empty in EVERY reuse sim: leg (b)'s "two --patch values" measures the kernel path, not a `git apply --index` shortcut, and M5 is already the shape of the normal case rather than a special sim.
- args.attentionPollMs is pinned to 600000 in the rig. The raised-hand poller is a SECOND getIssue on a timer, and leg (a) counts reads exactly-once-per-task; ten minutes puts it past every sim so the count measures the setup read and nothing else.
- The fake hub adds `status` per issue (M1's test is `status === "closed"`; kata-client's frozen projection has no closed_reason) and an `addLabel` method that test_worker_kata_env.mjs's fake lacks, so M3's "not marked needs-review" is an observation rather than a silent kata:write-failed.

payload.author: impl:2@run-132
payload.body:
Task 2 (reuse at setup) implemented and committed as 1ef60ad5 on top of BASE a595598a. Footprint: fleet/run-engine.mjs (+363/-), fleet/CONTRACT.md, fleet/tests/_engine_helpers.mjs — all inside FILES; fleet/tests/test_run_engine_reuse.mjs left untouched for the peer's exam.

Shape: the per-task getIssue moved out of runTaskInner into an openKataTask() called for every task at Setup (still exactly one read per task — test_worker_kata_env.mjs (c) pins that and stays green), answers kept in a kataIssues map. The reuse pass then runs between `rev-parse HEAD` and the baseline clone: closed + work.adopted_run + work.adopted_sha => reusable; one named run => fetch refs/tags/ultra/evidence/run-<M>, `git show` report.json and publish-fold/run.patch off the tag into <runDir>/reuse/, `git diff --binary parkedBase..BASE` as main.patch, then fold_wave.py fold --wave 0 --base <report.baseSha> --patch main= --patch reuse= and materialize --prev-head BASE. Every git verb goes through the engine exec seam in the integration clone; no worker prompt changed.

Three decisions worth recording:
1. materialize takes --prev-head BASE, not --prev-head report.baseSha. With the parked base the candidate is parented off that older commit and this run's BASE falls out of the ancestry; with BASE it is the single parent and the tree carries both sides. This matches publish-fold.mjs, which also passes the newer tip.
2. No `git apply --index` fallback for an empty main.patch. Measured against the real kernel: a 0-byte patch is a no-op task (repo_weave.apply_patch_tree documents it), fold and materialize both come out clean, so the kernel path always runs with two --patch values and M2's assertion holds in the BASE == parked-base case too.
3. Reused rows go into taskResults only, never into a wave's `results`. A reused row in `results` makes an all-reused wave look like it produced work, which trips the `!edgesSupplied && results.length > 0` cascade and blocks later waves — with taskResults only, such a wave takes the "merge skipped: no mergeable results" path and waveBaseSha stays the reuse head, which is what M3 asks for.

Also moved KERNEL/waveDirOf up beside `integ`: they were declared textually after Setup, so the reuse fold would have hit a TDZ ReferenceError.

Proofs, all green: test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs, test_worker_kata_env.mjs, the CONTRACT sed/grep, and the untouched-files git diff --quiet. Regression sweep also green: all 14 fleet/tests/test_*.mjs and tests/test_ultra_run.py + tests/test_fleet_suite.py (76 passed). Behaviour itself was driven end to end by a throwaway sim outside the repo (scratch-task-2/sim.mjs, not committed): happy path with BASE advanced past the parked base, the empty-set no-fetch case, and all four refusals.
